questions.q: Resistance of a wire at $0^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}, 100^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ and $t^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}$ is found to be $10 \Omega, 10.2 \Omega$ and $10.95 \Omega$ respectively. The temperature $t$ in Kelvin scale is _________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}=\mathrm{R}_0(1+\alpha \Delta \mathrm{T}) \\ & \frac{\Delta \mathrm{R}}{\mathrm{R}_0}=\alpha \Delta \mathrm{T}\end{aligned}$
Case-I
$\begin{aligned} & 0{ }^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C} \rightarrow 100^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C} \\ & \frac{10.2-10}{10}=\alpha(100-0)\end{aligned}$ ...(1)
Case-II
$0^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrmt^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C}\frac{10.95-10}{10}=\alpha(\mathrm{t}-0)$ ...(2)
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{t}}{100}=\frac{0.95}{0.2}=475^{{}^{{}^{\circ}}} \mathrm{C} \\ & \mathrm{t}=475+273=748 \mathrm{~K}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In the given circuit 'a' is an arbitrary constant. The value of $m$ for which the equivalent circuit resistance is minimum, will be $\sqrt{\dfrac{x}{2}}$. The value of $x$ is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Left part of the resistors are connected in parallel, hence& ${R}_{1} = \dfrac{am}{3}$.

Similarly, for the right part of the resistors we can write,~${R}_{2} = \dfrac{a}{2m}$.

Therefore, equivalent resistance will be,

$R = \dfrac{am}{3} + \dfrac{a}{2m}$

Differentiating both sides w.r.t~$m$~to observe critical points, we get~$\dfrac{dR}{dm} = \dfrac{a}{3} + \dfrac{a\left(- 1\right)}{2m^{2}} = 0$

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{3} = \dfrac{a}{2m^{2}}⇒ m = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}$

Thus,~$x = 3$.

questions.q: Two identical cells, when connected either in parallel or in series gives same current in an external resistance $5Ω$. The internal resistance of each cell will be ______~$Ω$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let& $r$~be the internal resistance of each cell.

In above shown figure, first represents the series connection of cells. Second and third figures represents the parallel connection~of cells.

Now, in case of series connection, ${ε}_{net} = 2εand{r}_{net} = 2r$. So, current~$i = \dfrac{2ε}{5 + 2r}$~.....(1)

In case of parallel~connection,~${ε}_{net} = \dfrac{εr + εr}{r + r} = εand{r}_{net} = \dfrac{r}{2}$. So, current~$i = \dfrac{ε}{\dfrac{r}{2} + 5}$~.....(2)

Equating (1) and (2), we get

$\dfrac{2ε}{5 + 2r} = \dfrac{ε}{\dfrac{r}{2} + 5}$

$⇒ r + 10 = 5 + 2r$

$⇒ r = 5Ω$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{eq}}=2 \Omega \\ & \mathrm{I}=\frac{2}{2}=1 \mathrm{~A}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
A meter bridge setup is shown in the figure. It is used to determine an unknown resistance $R$~using a given resistor of $15Ω$. The galvanometer \left(G\right)$ shows null defection when tapping key is at $43$ cm mark from end $A$. If the end correction for end $A$ is $2$ cm, then the determined value of $R$ will be $Ω$.

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Using the conditions of a balanced wheatstone bridge and adding the end correction.

$\dfrac{15}{R} = \dfrac{l + e}{\left(L + e\right) - \left(l + e\right)} ⇒ 15\left(43 + 2\right) = R\left(102 - 45\right) ⇒ R = \dfrac{57}{45} \times 15$

$⇒ R = 19Ω$

questions.q: In the experiment to determine the galvanometer resistance by half-deflection method, the plot of $1 / \theta$ vs the resistance $(\mathrm{R})$ of the resistance box is shown in the figure. The figure of merit of the galvanometer is _____ $\times 10^{-1} \mathrm{~A} /$ division. [The source has emf 2V]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & i=K \theta \\ & \frac{2}{G+R}=K \theta \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\theta}=\frac{(G+R) K}{2}=R\left(\frac{K}{2}\right)+\frac{K G}{2} \\ & \text { Slope }=\frac{K}{2}=\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow K=0.5=5 \times 10^{-1} A\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A cylindrical wire of radius $0 . 5mm$ and conductivity $5 \times {10}^{7}Sm^{- 1}$ is subjected to an electric field of $10mVm^{- 1} .$~The expected value of current in the wire will be $x^{3}\pimA .$~The value of $x$ is _________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Conductivity& $\sigma = 5 \times {10}^{7}Sm^{- 1}$

Radius~$r = 0 . 5mm = 5 \times {10}^{- 4}m$

$E = 10 \times {10}^{- 3}Vm^{- 1}$

$J = \sigmaE = 10 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 5 \times {10}^{7}$

$⇒ J = 5 \times {10}^{5}$

$⇒ \dfrac{i}{A} = 5 \times {10}^{5}$

$i = 5 \times {10}^{5} \times \pir^{2}$

$= 5 \times {10}^{5} \times \pi \times \left(5 \times {10}^{- 4}\right)2$

$= 125\pi \times {10}^{- 3}A$

Therefore,~$i = 125\pimA$

Hence,~$x = 5$

questions.q: As shown in the figure the voltmeter reads $2V$~across $5Ω$~resistor. The resistance of the voltmeter is _____ $Ω$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the resistance of the voltmeter be& $RΩ$. The voltmeter is in parallel with the~$5Ω$. So the total resistance in the circuit is~

\left(\dfrac{5R}{5 + R} + 2\right)Ω$

Applying Ohm's law in the whole circuit,~$V = IR$,

$I = \left(\dfrac{3}{2 + \dfrac{5R}{5 + R}}\right)A$

It is given that the potential difference across~$5Ω$~is~$2V$.

Thus, by Ohm's law,

\left(\dfrac{3}{2 + \dfrac{5R}{5 + R}}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{5R}{R + 5}\right) = 2 ⇒ \dfrac{15 + 3R}{10 + 7R} \times \dfrac{5R}{5 + R} = 2 ⇒ 15R = 20 + 14R ⇒ R = 20Ω$

In the figure given, the electric current flowing through the $5kΩ$ resistor is $x$~$mA$.

The value of $x$ to the nearest integer is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $I = \dfrac{21}{5 + 1 + 1} = 3mA$

questions.q:
The variation of applied potential and current flowing through a given wire is shown in figure. The length of wire is $31 . 4cm$. The diameter of wire is measured as $2 . 4cm$. The resistivity of the given wire is measured as $x \times {10}^{- 3}Ωcm$. The value of $x$ is _____ .

[Take $\pi = 3 . 14$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Since,& slope of V−I graph represents the resistance, so& $R = tan45 ° = 1Ω$

Now, resistance of wire is given by~$R = \dfrac{ρL}{A}$~

So, resistivity of the wire is~$ρ = \dfrac{A}{RL} = \dfrac{\pir^{2}}{RL} = \dfrac{\pi\left(1 . {2}^{2} \times {10}^{- 4}\right)}{31 . 4 \times {10}^{- 2}} = 1 . 44 \times {10}^{- 3}Ωm = 144 \times {10}^{- 3}Ωcm$

questions.q: Twelve wires each having resistance $2 \Omega$ are joined to form a cube. A battery of $6 \mathrm{~V}$ emf is joined across point $a$ and $c$. The voltage difference between $e$ and $f$ is ______V.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: From symmetry, current through e-b & g-d =0 $\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{R}_{\text {eq }}=\frac{3}{4} \times \mathrm{R}=\frac{3}{2} \Omega \\ & \therefore \text { Current through battery }=\frac{6 \times 2}{3}=4 \mathrm{~A} \\ & \mathrm{i}_2=\frac{4}{8} \times 2=1 \mathrm{~A} \\ & \therefore \Delta \mathrm{V} \text { across e-f }=\frac{\mathrm{i}_2}{2} \times \mathrm{R}=\frac{1}{2} \times 2=1 \mathrm{~V} \end{aligned}$

questions.q:
For the given circuit, in the steady state,& \left|{V}_{B} - {V}_{D}\right| =$~_____ $V$.

$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At steady state current will not pass through capacitor, therefore effective resistance between B and C will be only& $1Ω$. Modified circuit will be as shown below.

$⇒ {i}_{AB} = \dfrac{6}{3} = 2A$~ and ${i}_{AD} = \dfrac{6}{12} = 0 . 5A$

Applying Kirchoff's law along path BAD, we get

$⇒ {V}_{B} + \left(2 \times 2\right) - \left(10 \times 0 . 5\right) = {V}_{D}$

$⇒ {V}_{B} - {V}_{D} = 1V$.

questions.q: In the following circuit, the magnitude of current ${I}_{1}$, is ______~$A$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The figure above shows the current and voltage at different points in circuit.

Applying Kirchhoff's Junction law at $A$,

$\dfrac{x - ( y + 5 )}{1} + \dfrac{x - 2}{2} + \dfrac{x - 0}{2} = 0 . . . \left(1\right)$

Applying Kirchhoff's Junction law at $B$,

\dfrac{y + 5 - x}{1} + \dfrac{y - 0}{1} + \dfrac{y - 2}{1} =$0 . . . \left(2\right)$

Solving equation (1) and~(2), we get

$x = 3$~and~$y = 0$

Now, at~$D$~junction

${I}_{1} = {i}_{1} + {i}_{2}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = \dfrac{y - 0}{1} + \dfrac{x - 0}{2}$

$= \dfrac{0 - 0}{1} + \dfrac{3 - 0}{2}$

$⇒ {I}_{1} = 1 . 5A$.

questions.q: An electric bulb rated as $200W$ at $100V$ is used in a circuit having $200V$ supply. The resistance $R$~that must be put in series with the bulb so that the bulb delivers the same power is ______~$Ω$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Power, $P = \dfrac{V2}{RB}$

${R}_{B} = \dfrac{V2}{P} = \dfrac{100 \times 100}{200}$

${R}_{B} = 50Ω$

To produce same power, same voltage (i.e.,~$100V$) should be across the bulb.~

Hence, $R = {R}_{B}$

$R = 50Ω$

questions.q: Resistance are connected in a meter bridge circuit as shown in the figure. The balancing length ${l}_{1}$ is $40$ cm. Now an unknown resistance $x$ is connected in series with $P$ and new balancing length is found to be $80$ cm measured from the same end. Then the value of $x$ will be _____~$Ω$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Applying balanced condition for meter bridge

Initially, $\dfrac{P}{Q} = \dfrac{40cm}{60cm} = \dfrac{2}{3} . . . \left(1\right)$

Finally, \dfrac{P + x}{Q} = \dfrac{80cm}{20cm} = \dfrac{4}{1} . . . \left(2\right)$

Dividing equation~ \left(2\right)$ by ( \left(1\right)$,

\dfrac{P + x}{P} =$4 \times $\dfrac{3}{2} =$6$

$⇒ 1 + $\dfrac{x}{P} =$6 ⇒ $\dfrac{x}{P} =$5$

$∴ x = 5P = 5 \times 4 = 20Ω$

$

questions.q: The current flowing through the $1 \Omega$ resistor is $\frac{n}{10}$ A. The value of $n$ is _________
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{y-5}{2}+\frac{y-0}{2}+\frac{y-x+10}{1}=0 \\ & y-5+y+2 y-2 x+20=0 \\ & 4 y-2 x+15=0 \quad \ldots .(\text { (i) } \\ & \frac{x-5}{4}+\frac{x-0}{4}+\frac{x-10-y}{1}=0 \\ & x-5+x+4 x-40-4 y=0 \\ & 6 x-4 y-45=0 \quad . .(i) \\ & \frac{-2 x+4 y+15=0 . .(i i)}{4 x-30=0} \\ & x=\frac{15}{2} \& 4 y-15+15=0 \\ & y=0 \\ & i=\frac{y-x+10}{1} \\ & i=\frac{0-7.5+10}{1} \\ & i=2.5 A=\frac{n}{10} A \\ & n=25\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The length of a given cylindrical wire is increased to double of its original length. The percentage increase in the resistance of the wire will be _____& $%$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As volume is constant, so, length doubled and area reduces to half.

Resistance of a wire is given by& $R = \dfrac{ρl}{A}$, where,~$ρ$~is resistivity of a material.

Here,~${R}_{1} = \dfrac{ρl}{A}$~and~${R}_{2} = \dfrac{ρ\left(2l\right)}{\dfrac{A}{2}} = 4R$

So percentage increase in the resistance will be~$= \dfrac{4R - R}{R} \times 100 % = 300 %$

questions.q: When a resistance of $5Ω$~is shunted with a moving coil galvanometer, it shows a full scale deflection for a current of $250mA,$~however when $1050Ω$~resistance is connected with it in series, it gives full scale deflection for $25$ volt. The resistance of galvanometer is_________Ω .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the maximum current through the galvanometer, when a shunt resistance ${r}_{1}$~is connected is given by \left({i}_{G}\right)max = \dfrac{r1}{{r}_{1} + {R}_{G}}{i}_\max . . . \left(1\right)$

When a series~resistance~${r}_{2}$~is connected, the potential difference across the galvanometer is given by

$V = \left({i}_{G}\right)max \left[{R}_{G} + {r}_{2}\right] . . .\left(2\right)$

From equations (1) and (2), it can be written that

$\begin{cases}V \text{ and } = \text{ and } \dfrac{r1}{{r}_{1} + {R}_{G}}{i}_\max \left({R}_{G} + {r}_{2}\right)$\\ & ⇒ & V{r}_{1} + V{R}_{G} = {i}_\max{r}_{1}{R}_{G} + {i}_\max{r}_{1}{r}_{2} \\ & ⇒ & \left($V - {i}_\max{r}_{1}\right){R}_{G} = {i}_\max{r}_{1}{r}_{2} - V{r}_{1} \\ \text{ and } ⇒ \text{ and } {R}_{G} = $\dfrac{{i}_\max{r}_{1}{r}_{2} - V{r}_{1}}{V - {i}_\max{r}_{1}} . . . \left($3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required galvanometer resistance.

\begin{cases}{R}_{G}$ \text{ and } = \text{ and } $\dfrac{0 . 250A \times 5Ω \times 1050Ω - 25V \times 5Ω}{25V - 0 . 250A \times 5Ω}$\\ \text{ and } = \text{ and } 50Ω\end{cases}$

$

questions.q: An electrical bulb rated $220V, 100W$, is connected in series with another bulb rated $220V$, $60W$. If the voltage across combination is $220V$, the power consumed by the $100W$ bulb will be about _____~$W$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Electric power is given by& $P = \dfrac{V2}{R}$, here,~$V$~is voltage and~$R$~is resistance.

Now, for each bulb,~${R}_{1} = \dfrac{V2}{P} = \dfrac{2202}{100} = 484Ω$~and ${R}_{2} = \dfrac{V2}{P} = \dfrac{2202}{60} = 484\left(\dfrac{10}{6}\right)Ω$

Net current through the series combination is~$I = \dfrac{220}{484 + 484 \times \dfrac{10}{6}}A = 0 . 171A$

Hence, the power consumed by the $100W$ bulb is~${P}_{1} = I^{2}{R}_{1} = 14 . 06W$
